immigration.text: He calls for stronger border enforcement while also expanding legal pathways for temporary workers.
immigration.quote: Congress should expand legal pathways for the temporary workers our farms, mills, and businesses need. Secure the border, enforce the law fairly, and welcome those who come legally.

wages.text: She introduced legislation to index the federal minimum wage to regional costs of living.
wages.quote: Our bipartisan Fair Wage Act will make sure the minimum wage reflects economic realities on the ground in a dynamic way.

trade.text: She described tariffs as a policy tool whose effects depend on how they are used, while backing domestic manufacturing.
trade.quote: tariffs are a tool. A tool can be used destructively, or it can be used productively. And it depends on how it’s wielded.

debt.text: Her campaign says she supports strengthening Social Security without raising the retirement age or reducing benefits.
debt.quote: Marie supports common sense legislation to strengthen the Social Security program for the long-run without raising the retirement age or reducing benefits.

housing.text: She led the Build Now Act, which encourages localities to improve their housing-construction record and reduce permitting barriers.
housing.quote: Permitting and the red tape around housing has become so bloated and complicated that normal people can’t afford to build anything anymore.

safety.text: She supports funding law enforcement and boosting officer pay to improve retention.
safety.quote: Marie believes we need to provide more federal funding to boost officer and firefighter pay to improve retention

immigration.text: She called for comprehensive immigration legislation that provides border security while also creating legal pathways to citizenship.
immigration.quote: a bipartisan comprehensive immigration solution that delivers for our communities’ safety, migrants seeking legal pathways to citizenship, and our small businesses and farms facing acute labor shortages.

abortion.text: She says she is protecting abortion access and will work to prevent a national abortion ban.
abortion.quote: She is protecting access to critical medical care and the freedom of women to choose what is right for their families and themselves.

gender.text: She voted against passage of the 2025 Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act.
gender.quote: Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act

health.text: She voted against a law that reduced Medicaid eligibility and co-led legislation to extend Affordable Care Act premium tax credits.
health.quote: This law eliminated Medicaid eligibility for roughly 17 million Americans–including 31,000 in Southwest Washington.

energy.text: She said policy should support workers who rely on fossil fuels while transitioning to cleaner energy sources.
energy.quote: How do we reconcile the urgent need to support working-class Americans who rely on fossil fuels to get to work everyday with the imperative to transition to cleaner, more sustainable sources of energy?

voting.text: She voted for the SAVE Act while criticizing its provisions and affirming Washington’s vote-by-mail system.
voting.quote: I also understand the SAVE Act stands no chance of passage in the Senate due to the filibuster, as well as several deeply flawed provisions.
